data.label: Source Understanding
data.userPrompt:
You are analysing the SOURCE video of a short social reel that will be re-created ("cloned") with a different person and a brand's products. Watch AND listen to the whole video closely and report what you actually see and hear, concretely. Say "unsure" rather than guess.

1. WHAT DRIVES IT: in one or two sentences, the mechanic or idea that makes this video work, and the hook in the first second.
2. TIMELINE: every shot or beat with timestamps (start-end s): camera position and movement, framing, what the person does, props, outfit, and every cut or transition and how it is done.
3. PERSON AND STYLING: build and body type, age range, hair, makeup, styling, energy and expression. (Describe, don't identify.)
4. SETTING AND LOOK: location, set dressing, light (in plain words), colour palette, UGC phone footage or professional production.
5. ON-SCREEN TEXT AND GRAPHICS: every text or graphic with its timing, position, font feel, size, colour and animation. Say "none" if none.
6. MUSIC AND SOUND, like a music producer:
   - genre, sub-genre, scene or era
   - tempo in BPM (half-time or double-time feel?), and key if you can tell
   - every instrument and sound you hear and its role (lead, chords, bass, drums, percussion, ear candy)
   - vocals: none, sung, rapped, chopped, a vocal hook; language
   - structure with timestamps (intro, hook, build, drop, switch-ups) and where the energy changes
   - groove and drum pattern; mix character (warm or bright, lo-fi or polished, bass weight)
   - what the music does at each cut in the video
   - any sound effects or voice
   - if you recognise the track, name it here (this line only)
7. MUSIC PROMPT: ONE prompt under 80 words for a text-to-music model to make a NEW, original track in the same style, timed to this video's cuts. No artist names, no song titles. Concrete sounds only, no mood adjectives without a sound behind them.
8. WHAT A CLONE MUST KEEP: the 3 to 5 things that, if lost, would break the video.
